title: Dual-submission parallel computer architecture problem set
summary: Students first solve a parallel-computer-architecture problem set, receive instructor solutions, and then submit corrections and metacognitive explanations of their errors. Grading shifts emphasis from the initial answer to accurate self-assessment, correction, and reflection, reducing the incentive to outsource answers to an LLM.

sources.title: Dual-Submission Homework in Parallel Computer Architecture: An Exploratory Study in the Age of LLMs
sources.evidence_quote: They would receive the solutions soon after submitting their work, and then have an opportunity to correct it and resubmit.

assessment.summary: Submit answers to Problem Set 3, inspect released solutions, then correct errors and explain the reasoning failures in a second submission.
student_actions: Compare the first submission with instructor solutions.
Explain errors and rephrase corrections to demonstrate understanding.

student_role.description: The variant is designed to reduce the reward for obtaining initial answers from the web or an LLM; no explicit AI-use rule is reported.

assessment_system_role: Public solutions are deliberately released between submissions, moving assessed value to correction and reflection.

grading.method: Teaching assistants grade the two submissions together.

criteria.description: A correct first answer receives full credit.

reported_results: 93% wanted more homework using the dual-submission format.
Evidence of improved exam performance was inconclusive.
